title: Privileged representational axes in biological and artificial neural networks
title_zh: 生物与人工神经网络中的特权表征轴
abstract: How do neurons code information? Recent work emphasizes the geometry and information content of population codes, using measures that are blind to the native tunings (or 'axes') of neural responses. But might these representational axes matter, with some privileged systematically over others? We developed methods to test for alignment of neural tuning across brains and deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs). Across both vision and audition, both brains and DCNNs consistently favoured certain axes for representing the natural world. Moreover, the representational axes of DCNNs trained on natural inputs were aligned to those in perceptual cortices, such that axis-sensitive model-brain similarity metrics better differentiated competing models of biological sensory systems. We further show that coding schemes that privilege certain axes can facilitate task performance, reduce downstream wiring costs and improve generalization. These results motivate a new framework for understanding neural tuning in biological and artificial networks and its computational benefits.
abstract_zh: 神经元如何编码信息？最近的研究强调人群编码的几何结构和信息含量，使用的指标对神经反应的原生调谐（或‘轴’）一无所知。但这些表征轴是否重要，是否存在系统偏好的轴？我们开发了测试跨大脑和深度卷积神经网络（DCNN）神经调谐对齐的方法。在视觉和听觉中，大脑和DCNN都一致偏好某些轴来代表自然世界。此外，在感官皮层中，由自然输入训练的DCNN的表征轴与之对齐，这种轴敏感的模型-大脑相似度指标能更好地区分生物感官系统的竞争模型。我们进一步表明，优先考虑某些轴的编码方案可以促进任务性能，降低下游线路成本并提高泛化能力。这些结果激发了一个新的框架，用于理解生物网络和人工网络中神经调谐的计算优势。
